newsitem.title: UK: Britain's C&W to take control of Optus.
newsitem.headline: Britain's C&W to take control of Optus.

text.p: Cable and Wireless, Britain's second biggest telecoms company, said on Tuesday it planned to take financial as well as managerial control of Australian telephone carrier Optus Communications.

C&W, which already owned a 24.5 percent stake in Optus, ended weeks of speculation by announcing it had agreed to buy another 24.5 percent stake from America's BellSouth Corp for 445 million pounds ($740.6 million).
Optus will then simultaneously issue 298.9 million options, each entitling C&W to buy one newly-issued Optus share at an average estimated price of A$1.89.
"After exercise of the options, Cable & Wireless' shareholding in Optus would exceed 50 percent," the company said in a statement.
A spokesman said the agreement to raise its Optus stake to 51 or 52 percent depended on Australian government approval.

C&W said it planned to meet with the Australian government "in due course" to discuss its hopes for a relaxation of rules limiting foreign shareholders to 49 percent of Optus, Australia's second largest telecoms carrier.

As part of its deal with BellSouth, Cable and Wireless said it would transfer to the American group its 22.3 percent stake in OCCEL, the mobile operator in western Colombia -- subject to that company's agreement.
"This is a unique opportunity for us to manage Optus and add shareholder value," said C&W's chief executive Richard Brown.

"We have decided to dig our roots deeper into Australia where we can offer our customers a full range of integrated services, and plan to exit from a dilutive wireless business in Columbia, where we cannot."
C&W has already taken effective management control of Optus after former C&W executive Peter Howell-Davies was appointed chief executive officer at Optus earlier this month.
His predecessor, Ziggy Switkowski, resigned after a year of rising losses at Optus's pay television operations.

"As a high growth, fully integrated telecommunications, information and entertainment company Optus fits well with our view of the future," said Brown. "Optus is already a successful business, growing market share in a highly competitive Australian market.
"More hard work lies ahead but, now that we can manage the company, we can apply our unrivalled experience in broadband communications around the world."
